meta.title: Code of Conduct
meta.description: The ADA Code of Conduct for certified doulas: professional standards, client care principles and ethical guidelines, and how to report a concern.

title: Standards, conduct and complaints
lead: Every ADA-certified doula agrees to the ADA Code of Conduct. Anyone can report a concern. Suspensions and revocations show on the doula’s public record.

conduct.title: Code of Conduct
conduct.intro: As an ADA-certified doula, you are expected to uphold the highest standards of professional and ethical conduct. This Code of Conduct outlines the principles that guide our certified doulas in providing exceptional, culturally sensitive care.
conduct.count: The Code has {count} principles, in the groups below.
conduct.photoAlt: A trainee changes a training doll’s diaper during an ADA Postpartum Doula Program session
conduct.photoCaption: Newborn care practice on a training doll. ADA training, August 2024.
conduct.competencyText: Maintain professional competency through ongoing education and stay current with best practices in postpartum care.
conduct.scopeText: Provide only services you are trained and certified to offer. Refer clients to appropriate clinicians for medical concerns outside a doula’s scope.
conduct.certificationsText: Keep ADA certification current through timely renewal and continuing education requirements.
conduct.communicationText: Communicate clearly, respectfully, and honestly with clients, their families, and the broader care team.
conduct.clientCenteredText: Center the client’s needs, values, and choices in every aspect of care, honoring their autonomy and lived experience.
conduct.consentText: Provide clear information so clients can make informed decisions about their care, always seeking consent before acting.
conduct.confidentialityText: Protect client privacy. Do not share personal, medical, or family information without explicit, written consent.
conduct.nonDiscriminationText: Serve all families equitably, regardless of race, ethnicity, religion, language, family structure, sexual orientation, or gender identity.
conduct.culturalText: Honor each family’s cultural traditions and integrate them thoughtfully with evidence-based postpartum care.
conduct.integrityText: Represent credentials, experience, and scope of practice honestly. Avoid misleading claims in marketing and consultations.
conduct.conflictText: Disclose any potential conflicts of interest to clients and act in their best interest at all times.
conduct.boundariesText: Maintain clear professional boundaries with clients and their families, even in the intimate setting of postpartum care.
conduct.reportingText: Report concerns about abuse, neglect, or safety risks in accordance with applicable laws and ADA policy.
conduct.accountabilityText: Accept responsibility for professional conduct and cooperate with ADA review processes when concerns arise.
conduct.enforcement: Violations of this Code of Conduct may result in disciplinary action, including suspension or revocation of ADA certification.

scope.title: Scope of practice
scope.intro: ADA-certified doulas give non-medical support. They refer medical concerns to clinicians.
scope.postpartumText: Supports the family at home in the weeks after the birth: newborn care, feeding, the parent’s recovery and the household’s adjustment.
scope.birthText: Supports the family during labor and delivery.
scope.medicalText: Refer them to the family’s clinicians. Doula support is non-medical.

report.title: Report a concern
report.intro: Anyone can report a concern about an ADA-certified doula: a family, a client, another doula or an agency. If you become aware of a potential violation of this Code of Conduct, please report it to ADA at <mail>{email}</mail>.
report.caption: Which concerns ADA reviews
report.breach: A possible breach of the Code of Conduct by an ADA-certified doula
report.dispute: A billing or contract dispute between a family and an agency or employer
report.notCertified: Care given by someone who is not ADA-certified
report.notCertifiedWhere: <link>Check the registry</link> first: the person may not hold an ADA credential.
report.note: All reports will be reviewed confidentially.

cta.title: Anyone can report a concern about an ADA-certified doula.
